environment.jvmArguments: the default of the Quarkus fast-jar and of the gateway's start script

workload.requestIds: w53-bench-<runStamp>-<index> — unique per run, because chain A's cognitive database is persistent and a request id is the identity of a dispatch
workload.payloadSize: one sentence of input and one expectation
workload.seed: none — the workload has no randomness
workload.procedure: the tasks go through POST /v1/cognitive/task on chain A, as many at a time as the concurrency allows; the latency is the client's round trip, the stage times are chain A's own monotonic measurements of the parts it can time

stageMeanings.intent_written_nanos: chain A: the durable dispatch intent, written before the send
stageMeanings.dispatch_nanos: chain A: signing the request, the network round trip, chain B's authentication, its durable inbox write, the production inference, the signed answer and its verification
stageMeanings.peer_execution_nanos: chain B, as chain B measured it: the production inference itself, rounded to the millisecond; the difference against dispatch_nanos is the network, the signing and chain B's own bookkeeping
stageMeanings.report_admission_nanos: chain A: the report entering the epistemic model through chain A's own bridge receiver
stageMeanings.assessment_nanos: chain A: the epistemic evaluation of the answer
stageMeanings.total_nanos: chain A: the whole task, as chain A can see it
stageMeanings.replay_dispatch_nanos: the replay path: chain A sending the request again and the peer answering from its durable record
stageMeanings.replay_report_admission_nanos: the replay path: the report entering the epistemic model again
stageMeanings.replay_assessment_nanos: the replay path: the epistemic evaluation again
stageMeanings.replay_total_nanos: the replay path: the whole replay, as chain A can see it

processMetricsMeanings.chainA: the Quarkus application: the CPU time it used, the peak memory it held, and the garbage collection the JVM's own log records
processMetricsMeanings.chainB: the gateway's JDK server: the CPU time it used and the peak memory it held
processMetricsMeanings.cpuSecondsPerTask: the CPU time the two processes together spent on the first pass, divided by the number of tasks
processMetricsMeanings.cpuSecondsPerReplay: the CPU time the two processes together spent on the replay pass, divided by the number of replays
processMetricsMeanings.estimatedAllocationBytes: the heap the JVM collected during the run, plus the growth of the heap it held — an estimate of the allocation, not a counter of it
processMetricsMeanings.allocationIsLowerBound: true when the JVM collected nothing during the run: the estimate is then a lower bound on the allocation
processMetricsMeanings.retainedResidentBytes: the growth of the resident set over the run — the memory the run retained in the process
processMetricsMeanings.peakResidentBytes: the peak of the whole lifetime of the process, the startup included; it is not the memory the run used

whatThisReportDoesNotClaim: it does not claim a p99 from a sample of this size

it does not separate chain B's stages from the network round trip — chain A times the crossing as one interval, and only the peer's own total is told apart, by the duration the peer reports; the peer's authentication, its durable inbox write and its answer signing are still inside the crossing
it does not claim that these numbers are comparable with a run on another machine
no optimization was accepted on the strength of this run alone
it does not claim an exact allocation per task: the allocation is estimated from the JVM's own garbage-collection log, and the estimate is named as an estimate
it does not separate the serialization and the signature cost from the network round trip — chain A times the crossing as one interval

it does not claim that the replay path avoided the peer entirely: the request is sent again and the peer answers from its durable record, and the report measures that path rather than asserting that it never reached the peer
it does not average the two workloads into one number: they answer different questions, and each keeps its own section
